assessment.summary: CD274 (PD-L1) is a highly druggable immune checkpoint target with exceptional structural, chemical, and clinical validation. Five approved antibody drugs exist, over 1700 IC50 entries are recorded in ChEMBL with a median of ~210 nM, and 20 high-resolution PDB structures (best 0.99 Å) including 13 ligand-bound complexes confirm a well-characterised binding interface. Active research continues across multiple cancer types, solidifying its status as a premier immuno-oncology target.
evidence_gaps: Small-molecule inhibitors remain challenging due to the flat protein-protein interaction surface; most approved agents are monoclonal antibodies, leaving oral small-molecule druggability only partially established
Resistance mechanisms to existing PD-L1 blockade are not fully elucidated, limiting next-generation drug design
Biomarker strategies for patient stratification (e.g., which tumour types and PD-L1 expression thresholds predict response) remain an active and unresolved area
Intracellular and non-canonical signalling roles of CD274 are not comprehensively characterised and may reveal additional druggable modalities
Data on combination partner optimisation and sequencing with other checkpoint inhibitors is still evolving
